reason: The cited evidence (E1) only states that a FeCrNiTiZr HEA coating was fabricated on H13 steel, has high hardness and good elevated temperature wear resistance, and can be used as a repair material. It does not mention laser cladding, hot cracking reduction, the specific composition, dual-phase microstructure, rapid solidification effects, or quantitative comparisons to fusion welding. The key premises are therefore largely unsupported by the provided evidence.
premises: Laser cladding of FeCrNiTiZr HEA on H13 steel reduces hot cracking
The specific composition (Fe 32, Cr 25, Ni 25, Ti 10, Zr 8 wt%) yields a dual-phase BCC+FCC/eutectic microstructure
Rapid solidification refines microstructure and limits hot crack formation
The coating provides over 20% increase in microhardness and improved wear resistance over fusion welds
The coating is an excellent repair material for H13 tool steel
